problem: The single range 1700–2000 °C is low for an air–acetylene flame, which is usually quoted near 2200–2300 °C; that range fits air–LPG better.
fix: Say: an air–acetylene flame at about 2200–2300 °C, or an air–LPG flame at about 1700–2000 °C.

where: Section 3, internal standard paragraph, and Quiz Q5
problem: The internal-standard ratio is described only as sodium-to-lithium, so a student can conclude the lithium standard helps only sodium measurements, while the chapter also measures potassium.
fix: State that when sodium is measured the instrument uses the sodium-to-lithium ratio, and when potassium is measured it uses the potassium-to-lithium ratio; flame flicker and spray-rate changes cancel in either ratio.

problem: The note says the sample is diluted 1:50 in water, but Section 3 says an internal lithium standard is added to every sample, which in practice means the diluent contains lithium.
fix: Change the note to '1:50 in lithium-containing diluent' so the figure agrees with the internal-standard method.

problem: Potassium is read at 766 nm, which is in the near-infrared, but the chapter never says the photodetector must respond at that wavelength; a student may assume any detector used for the yellow sodium line also suits potassium.
fix: Add one sentence: the detector must be sensitive at the chosen line, including the near-infrared 766 nm potassium line.
